TD(0)

Monte Carlo (Lesson 35) waits until the episode ends to learn anything. Temporal-difference learning updates after every step: it moves $V(S_t)$ towards the reward it just got plus its own estimate of the state it landed in. It learns a guess from a guess.

S&B Example 6.2. Start in C, step left or right with equal chance. Exiting right pays $1$; every other step pays $0$. Green fill is $V(s)$, the dashed line is the true value.

The maths

The value of a state is an expected return, and the return splits into one reward plus the rest (Lesson 25):

$$v_\pi(s) = \mathbb{E}_\pi\big[G_t \mid S_t = s\big] = \mathbb{E}_\pi\big[R_{t+1} + \gamma\, v_\pi(S_{t+1}) \,\big|\, S_t = s\big]$$

The value now is the expected reward plus the discounted value of wherever the agent goes next.

Monte Carlo samples the left-hand form, $G_t$. DP computes the right-hand form exactly with a model. TD(0) samples the right-hand form: one real step gives $R_{t+1}$ and $S_{t+1}$, and the unknown $v_\pi(S_{t+1})$ is replaced by the current estimate:

$$V(S_t) \leftarrow V(S_t) + \alpha\big[\underbrace{R_{t+1} + \gamma V(S_{t+1})}_{\text{TD target}} - V(S_t)\big]$$

Each step moves the estimate a fraction $\alpha$ of the way towards the TD target. A terminal state has value $0$.

For the random walk ($\gamma = 1$), each inner state's true value is the average of its neighbours, with $0$ beyond A and $1$ beyond E:

$$v_\pi(k) = \tfrac12\, v_\pi(k-1) + \tfrac12\, v_\pi(k+1), \quad v_\pi(0) = 0,\; v_\pi(6) = 1 \;\Rightarrow\; v_\pi(k) = \tfrac{k}{6}$$

So A to E are worth $\tfrac16, \tfrac26, \tfrac36, \tfrac46, \tfrac56$: the probability of exiting on the right.

For a fixed policy, tabular TD(0) converges to $v_\pi$ in the mean for a small enough constant $\alpha$, and with probability 1 if $\alpha$ decreases according to the usual stochastic approximation conditions ($\sum \alpha_n = \infty$, $\sum \alpha_n^2 < \infty$; S&B §6.2). With a constant $\alpha$ the estimates keep jittering around the true values, as the RMS error shows.
